messages:
alex: Heads-up — RFC follow-up: proposal to extract stateful adapters (session-store, kv-cache) out of runtime to a separate stateful-adapter layer. Want a short checklist and migration plan. TL;DR: aims to reduce runtime surface and make hotpath stateless.

maria: Curious about latency tradeoffs. won't extra network hop spike p50/p99?

sam: Agree. We should measure. Quick sim showed +3ms p50, +12ms p99 for 2% of tails. But allows better autoscaling.

lee: Data migration is the hairy part. Sessions currently live in runtime memory and redis fallback. Need joiners for live sessions.

alex: Right. Plan idea:
- phase 0: sidecar stateful-adapter behind feature-flag
- phase 1: cut runtime writes, read fallback bridges
- phase 2: lift traffic with canary rollout
- phase 3: decommission legacy state path

sam: Add metrics to track session mismatch, stale reads, error rates. Also add strict schema checks.

jen: Are we going to change the session API? we should keep X-Session-Id header semantics. Also support idempotency keys.

alex: No API break. We'll keep headers and include 'X-Adapter-Version' for observability.

maria: Ops: storage sizing needed. If stateful-adapter takes writes, we need capacity plans and GC TTL defaults.

infra-bot: FYI quota check: default Redis cluster has 500k keys in us-west-2. Link: http://go/infra/redis-quotas

lee: Migration approach idea:
1) dual-write to runtime+adapter (feature flag)
2) background sync to reconcile
3) read-after-write favor adapter once synced

sam: For consistency, we can use a short grace TTL (30s) for runtime cache to avoid stale reads during cutover.

alex: Canary plan: start with 1% traffic on dedicated canary shard. Monitor latency, error, session-mismatch. Rollforward if <0.5% mismatch and p99 delta < 10ms.

maria: Tests: end-to-end smoke with long-running sessions, chaos injection (broker restarts), perf bench.

jen: Docs: DevEx needs a migration guide and updated SDK with 'statefulAdapter' option.

alex: Owners:
- alex: overall plan + canary
- lee: migration tool + reconciliation
- sam: perf tests + metrics
- jen: docs + SDK changes

maria: +1 on owners. timeline?

alex: Rough: spike 2w, dual-write 3w, canary 2w, full cutover 2w. total ~9w.

sam: risk: cross-region latency for session reads. consider local adapter per region fallback.

alex: Noted. We'll add regional placement to requirements.

maria: +:thumbsup: I'll schedule an RFC follow-up sync tomorrow 10am. invite: @sam @lee @jen

infra-bot: Calendar event created: "Stateful Adapter Migration sync" 10:00 tomorrow.

alex: Thanks all. I'll post a short checklist doc in #architecture after the sync: http://go/notes/stateful-adapter-checklist
